title: Lola Young Announces 2027 Everything Begins Tour
excerpt: Lola Young has announced the Everything Begins Tour, a 17-date North American headline run scheduled for spring 2027.
body:
Lola Young has announced the Everything Begins Tour, a 17-date North American headline run scheduled for spring 2027. The tour opens at The Pinnacle in Nashville on April 6 and closes at the Greek Theatre in Los Angeles on May 4, giving Young her first full headline run across the United States and Canada since she stepped away from touring in 2025.

The itinerary includes Radio City Music Hall in New York, two nights at Massey Hall in Toronto and the Bill Graham Civic Auditorium in San Francisco. The New York and Los Angeles shows are among the largest U.S. headline rooms Young has booked to date. The tour name comes from her "Everything Ends" tattoo, reversing the phrase for a run that arrives after a year spent returning to regular live work.

Young rebuilt her stage schedule gradually during 2026. "Messy" won Best Pop Solo Performance at the Grammy Awards in February, and she later returned to major festival stages including Rock in Rio, Reading and Austin City Limits. Those appearances put her back in front of large crowds without immediately replacing the long stretch of headline dates that disappeared from her calendar in 2025.

New music followed in May with "From Down Here," her first original single since *I'm Only F**king Myself*. Produced by James Blake, the song was written the day after Young's Grammy win. It arrived as her live schedule was beginning to grow again, giving the return a new recording of its own rather than extending the cycle around "Messy" alone.

Sofia and the Antoinettes will support the announced North American dates. Artist presales begin October 7, followed by the general sale on October 9 at 10 a.m. local time through Young's official site.

The 2027 schedule restores the North American headline run that disappeared from Young's calendar in 2025, now with larger venues and new music in the set. Radio City Music Hall, two nights at Massey Hall and the Greek Theatre make the change in scale clear without turning the announcement into a list of every stop.
